matches.description: Watch Inter vs Parma highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 3, 2026. On May 3, 2026 , the San Siro played host to a pivotal Serie A clash as Inter Milan looked to maintain their momentum against a gritty Parma Calcio 1913 . The atmosphere was electric, with both sets of fans aware that this late-season fixture could prove decisive for their respective league ambitions. Early Pressure and the Breakthrough From the opening whistle, Inter sought to establish dominance through wide play and set-piece situations. Federico Dimarco was particularly active, delivering a succession of dangerous corners in the 2nd, 10th, and 22nd minutes. While the Parma defense held firm during these initial waves of pressure, the home side nearly found the opener in the 7th minute. Marcus Thuram rose highest to meet a cross, directing a powerful header toward goal, but Zion Suzuki was well-positioned to make a comfortable save. Parma struggled to find an attacking rhythm, often seeing their advances halted by the assistant referee's flag, with Enrico Del Prato and Gabriel Strefezza both caught in offside positions during the first half. As the match approached the interval, Inter finally breached the visitors' resistance. In the first minute of stoppage time, Piotr Zielinski turned provider, threading a precise ball through to Marcus Thuram . The French forward made no mistake, clinicaly finishing with his right foot to send the home support into raptures. It was a cruel blow for Parma , who had defended stoutly for the majority of the period only to concede at the very last moment before the break. Reinforcements and the Final Blow The second half saw a more physical contest, punctuated by a yellow card for Piotr Zielinski in the 64th minute for a mistimed challenge. Sensing the need for fresh energy to put the game to bed, the Inter coaching staff opted for a double substitution shortly after, introducing Henrikh Mkhitaryan and Lautaro Martinez for Zielinski and Thuram . The tactical shift paid dividends almost immediately. In the 80th minute, the two substitutes combined beautifully; Lautaro Martinez provided a selfless assist to Henrikh Mkhitaryan , who was left with an easy left-footed tap-in to double the lead. Parma refused to surrender, making several attacking changes of their own, including the introduction of Pontus Almqvist and Nesta Elphege . They nearly clawed their way back into the game in the 89th minute when Hans Nicolussi Caviglia swung a corner into the box, but Elphege ’s header drifted agonizingly wide of the post. It was the closest the visitors would come to challenging the scoreline as Inter ’s defensive discipline remained intact. Defined by Control and Late Drama The closing stages of the match were defined by Inter 's superior game management and ball retention, maintaining 59% possession to starve Parma of any late opportunities. Despite the two-goal cushion, the hosts continued to push for more. In the final minute of regulation time, Davide Frattesi —who had replaced Nicolo Barella —hit a fierce volley on target, but Zion Suzuki produced another fine save to keep the margin at two. Even deep into injury time, the intensity remained high. Franco Carboni was penalized for a trip on Denzel Dumfries , and Alessandro Circati was forced into a desperate clearance to prevent a third goal. When the final whistle eventually sounded after four minutes of added time, Inter celebrated a deserved victory built on a foundation of clinical finishing and tactical depth. For Parma , it was a night of missed half-chances and frustration, as they were unable to convert their 41% possession into meaningful threats against a disciplined Milanese outfit.

The Serie A clash between Inter and Verona on May 17, 2026, provided a masterclass in tactical discipline and late-game unpredictability. The match unfolded as a classic encounter between a dominant force and a resilient underdog, keeping fans on the edge of their seats until the very last whistle. Nerazzurri Dominance and the Opening Breakthrough From the outset, Inter established a stranglehold on the match, commanding a staggering 75% of ball possession. Petar Sucic was the focal point of their creative efforts, delivering a relentless series of corners that tested the Verona backline. While the first half remained goalless despite the pressure—with Yann Sommer comfortably handling headers from Nicolas Valentini and Sandi Lovric —the deadlock was finally broken in the 47th minute. An unfortunate own goal by Andrias Edmundsson gave Inter the lead they had been searching for, setting the stage for what seemed like a routine victory. Stoppage Time Twists and Turns As the clock ticked down, Inter introduced fresh legs, including Piotr Zielinski and Federico Dimarco , while Raffaele Di Gennaro replaced Sommer in goal. The hosts nearly doubled their lead in the 86th minute when a goal-bound shot from Petar Sucic was heroically hacked off the line by the Verona defense. This goal-line clearance proved to be a turning point, as it kept the visitors within striking distance. In the first minute of added time, the narrative shifted dramatically. Kieron Bowie found space in the box and unleashed a left-footed strike that found the back of the net, leveling the score at 1-1. Verona even threatened a late winner through Ioan Vermesan , whose header flashed wide, but the final whistle confirmed a dramatic draw that felt like a victory for the visitors and a missed opportunity for the dominant hosts.

With both sides eager to establish dominance in the league standings, the match promised a tactical chess match from the opening whistle. Inter Take Charge Early On May 4, 2026 , Inter wasted no time asserting their authority on home turf. The deadlock was broken just six minutes in when Marcus Thuram delivered a pinpoint ball to Lautaro Martinez , who connected with a superb right-footed volley to send the stadium into raptures. The early goal allowed the Nerazzurri to dictate the tempo, leaving Lazio struggling to find their rhythm. As the first half drew to a close, the hosts doubled their advantage through a moment of individual brilliance. In the 39th minute, Petar Sucic picked up a pass from Andy Diouf and unleashed a powerful left-footed strike from outside the penalty area. The ball flew past the keeper, providing Inter with a comfortable cushion heading into the break. Red Card and Final Blow Lazio attempted to find a way back into the contest in the second half, but their mountain became even steeper in the 59th minute. Following a VAR review, Alessio Romagnoli was shown a straight red card for a serious foul, leaving the visitors shorthanded. Despite being a man down, Gustav Isaksen nearly pulled one back for the Biancocelesti, only to see his goal-bound effort hacked off the line by the alert Inter defense. Any hopes of a comeback were extinguished in the 76th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny turned provider, setting up Henrikh Mkhitaryan for a clinical left-footed finish to make it three. The final stages saw Inter professionally see out the game, with Petar Sucic earning plaudits for a Man of the Match-caliber performance that secured a convincing victory for the home side.

In just the 6th minute, the visitors broke the deadlock with a clinical team move. Yann Aurel Bisseck initiated the play that found Marcus Thuram , who provided the delivery for Lautaro Martinez . The Argentine captain made no mistake, volleying the ball into the back of the net with his right foot to give his side the perfect start. Lazio struggled to find their rhythm as the Nerazzurri defense held firm. The pressure from the visitors told again in the 39th minute when they doubled their lead. Petar Sucic , who would go on to be a standout performer, received an assist from Lautaro Martinez and unleashed a powerful left-footed strike from outside the box. The ball flew past the keeper, leaving the home side with a mountain to climb before the interval. Red Card Drama and Lazio's Struggle The second half saw tactical adjustments from both sides, but the complexion of the game changed drastically in the 59th minute. Following a serious foul, Alessio Romagnoli was initially shown a yellow card, but after a VAR review, the referee upgraded the decision to a straight red. Reduced to ten men, Lazio faced an uphill battle to salvage anything from the encounter. Despite the disadvantage, the home side nearly pulled one back in the 61st minute. Gustav Isaksen managed to get a shot away, but his effort was heroically hacked off the goal line by the Inter defense. The visitors then utilized their numerical superiority to control possession, effectively suffocating any potential comeback attempt from the Roman club. Mkhitaryan Seals the Points Any hope of a late miracle for the hosts was extinguished in the 76th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny , introduced as a substitute, turned provider for Henrikh Mkhitaryan . The veteran midfielder found space and fired a left-footed shot into the net to make it 3-0.
